about: One scalar outcome per Agents 101 module: the share of students who can state the module's one target idea cold, in their own words. Target = the module's Big Idea, phrased as the take-home a student would say. Everything else (story judge, taste, flags, other learnings, mood) is a guard rail. The scorer never sees which module the student took: it must pick this target out of all eight, or 'none'.
cold_question: A colleague missed this module. In one or two sentences, what is the one idea from it they should not miss?

modules.target: Give the agent your own guardrails (a framework you know, your own facts and taste) and the output becomes recognizably yours instead of generic.
A system of files the agent reads and updates, plus automation, remembers and keeps getting better; a chat forgets every time.
Several agents can split the work and coordinate through shared files: the filesystem is their meeting room.
You cannot tell from the agent's output whether it is safe; run a repeatable check (assess, mitigate, reassess what is left, decide) instead of waiting for certainty.
Do not pick a quality check on faith: run several on your own output, score them against a benchmark, and keep the one that wins.
Keep the judge fixed and separate from what generates the work; then the score means something and the loop can improve the work without you in every round.
You cannot really share an agent; you share its context, a skill, its output or an interface, and choosing which one is a decision about your team.
The tool that builds tools compounds: your agent can build new agents that extend your own system.
